'''Jameel Sadik''' '''Al-Khalili''' ({{langx|ar|جميل صادق الخليلي}}; born 20 September 1962)<ref name="whoswho" /> is an Iraqi-British [[theoretical physicist]] and science populariser. He is a professor of theoretical physics and chair in the public engagement in science at the [[University of Surrey]]. He is a regular broadcaster and presenter of science programmes on [[BBC]] radio and television and a frequent commentator about science in other British media.

In 2014, Al-Khalili was named a RISE (Recognising Inspirational Scientists and Engineers) leader by the UK's [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.epsrc.ac.uk/newsevents/news/2014/Pages/riseawards.aspx/ |title=RISE Awards Announced |work=EPSRC |date=31 March 2014 |access-date=8 April 2014 |archive-date=11 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140611040453/http://www.epsrc.ac.uk/newsevents/news/2014/Pages/riseawards.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="scopus" /> He was president of [[Humanists UK]] between January 2013 and January 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://humanism.org.uk/2012/12/14/jim-al-khalili-named-president-elect-of-british-humanist-association/ |work=British Humanist Association |title=Jim Al-Khalili named President-elect of British Humanist Association |date=14 December 2012 |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=16 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116232850/http://humanism.org.uk/2012/12/14/jim-al-khalili-named-president-elect-of-british-humanist-association/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/profile/jimalkhalili Jim Al-Khalili] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410232717/https://www.theguardian.com/profile/jimalkhalili |date=10 April 2021 }} at ''[[The Guardian]]''</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fzKzJGmYq3o Lecture on Alan Turing] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411022157/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fzKzJGmYq3o |date=11 April 2021 }} from the University of Edinburgh YouTube Channel. Posted 4 June 2012. Retrieved 28 April 2017.</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Al-Khalili was born in [[Baghdad]] in 1962.<ref name="whoswho" /> His father was an [[Iraqi Air Force]] engineer with Arab heritage<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/profiles/5v9Pb2sZg2gz4HFGvsmtl2N/jim-al-khalili|title=Jim Al-Khalili|website=BBC Radio 4|access-date=14 June 2026|archive-date=12 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112115519/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/profiles/5v9Pb2sZg2gz4HFGvsmtl2N/jim-al-khalili|url-status=live}}</ref> from [[Najaf]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://newhumanist.org.uk/articles/facing-the-future-an-interview-with-jim-al-khalili/|title=Facing the future: an interview with Jim Al-Khalili|website=New Humanist|date=7 March 2013|access-date=14 June 2026|archive-date=7 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260607081053/https://newhumanist.org.uk/articles/facing-the-future-an-interview-with-jim-al-khalili/|url-status=live}}</ref> and his [[English people|English]] mother was a librarian.<ref name=tlsj>{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Rutherford|author-link=Adam Rutherford|year=2019|title=Jim Al-Khalili on HIS life scientific|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0002bml|publisher=BBC|access-date=7 February 2019|archive-date=15 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210715035819/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0002bml|url-status=live}}</ref> Al-Khalili settled permanently in the [[United Kingdom]] in 1979.<ref name="whoswho" /> 

After completing (and retaking) his [[GCE Advanced Level (United Kingdom)|A-levels]] over three years until 1982,<ref name=tlsj /> he studied [[physics]] at the University of Surrey and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1986. He stayed on at Surrey to pursue a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in nuclear reaction theory, which he obtained in 1989, rather than accepting a job offer from the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]].<ref name="jimphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Jameel |last=Al-Khalili |title=Intermediate Energy Deuteron Elastic Scattering from Nuclei in a Three-Body Model |publisher=University of Surrey |year=1989 |url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.328117 |id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.328117}} |author-link=Jim Al-Khalili |oclc=556478831 |archive-date=26 February 2021 |access-date=21 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226151730/https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.328117 |url-status=live }} {{free access}} {{registration required}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
[[File:Jim Al-Khalili QED.jpg|thumbnail|Al-Khalili talking about [[determinism]] at QED 2011]]
In 1989, Al-Khalili was awarded a [[Science and Engineering Research Council]] (SERC) postdoctoral fellowship at [[University College London]], after which he returned to Surrey in 1991, first as a research assistant, then as a lecturer.<ref>{{cite web|title=University of Surrey: Professor Jim Al-Khalili|url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/physics/people/jim_al-khalili/|access-date=2 November 2013|archive-date=22 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222140156/https://www.surrey.ac.uk/physics/people/jim_al-khalili/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1994, Al-Khalili was awarded an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]] Advanced Research Fellowship for five years,<ref name="epsrc" /> during which time he established himself as a leading expert on mathematical models of [[hypernucleus|exotic atomic nuclei]]. He has published widely in his field.<ref name="googlescholar">{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref>[https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7003459889 ''Al-Khalili, Jim S.'' Author details] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920122926/https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7003459889 |date=20 September 2021 }}, [[Scopus]]</ref>

Al-Khalili is a professor of physics at the [[University of Surrey]], where he also holds a chair in the Public Engagement in Science.<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Jim Al-Khalili OBE, theoretical physicist, University of Surrey |url=https://www.theguardian.com/open-weekend/professor-jim-al-khalili-obe |date=2 February 2012 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=8 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308153212/https://www.theguardian.com/open-weekend/professor-jim-al-khalili-obe |url-status=live }}</ref> He has been a trustee (2006–2012) and vice president (2008–2011) of the [[British Science Association]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org/people/jim-al-khalili/ |title=Professor Jim Al-Khalili OBE |work=Royal Society |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=3 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103193438/http://royalsociety.org/people/jim-al-khalili/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also held an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] Senior Media Fellowship.<ref name="epsrc">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UGYe300kyXUC&q=Engineering%20and%20Physical%20Sciences%20Research%20Council%20Al-Khalili&pg=PT74 |first=Laura |last=Bowater |title=Science Communication: A Practical Guide for Scientists |year=2012 |page=74|publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-118-40666-3 }}</ref>

Al-Khalili was awarded the [[Royal Society of London Michael Faraday Prize]] for science communication for 2007<ref>{{cite news |last=Al-Khalili |first=Jim |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2008/jan/30/religion.world |title=The Arabic Science That Prefigured Newton |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |location=England |date=21 January 2008 |access-date=17 March 2009 |archive-date=11 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210911105403/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2008/jan/30/religion.world |url-status=live }}</ref> and elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[British Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He has been a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] since 2000, when he also received the Institute's Public Awareness of Physics Award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thersa.org/large-text/events/speakers-archive/a/jim-al-khalili |title=RSA – Jim Al-Khalili |access-date=2 November 2013 |work=[[Royal Society of Arts]] |archive-date=4 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104013757/http://www.thersa.org/large-text/events/speakers-archive/a/jim-al-khalili |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has lectured widely both in the UK and around the world, particularly for the [[British Council]]. He is a member of the British Council Science and Engineering Advisory Group,<ref>{{cite web |title=Biographies of Science and Engineering Advisory Group members |url=http://www.britishcouncil.org/new/PageFiles/4487/Science_advisory_groups181109.pdf |work=British Council |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=23 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923222907/http://www.britishcouncil.org/new/PageFiles/4487/Science_advisory_groups181109.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> a member of the [[Royal Society]] Equality and Diversity Panel,<ref>{{cite web |work=The Royal Society |title=Equality and Diversity Advisory Network |url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/governance/committees/equality-diversity/ |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=2 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402190506/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/governance/committees/equality-diversity/ |url-status=live }}</ref> an external examiner for the [[Open University]] Department of Physics and Astronomy, a member of the Editorial Board for the open access Journal PMC Physics A, and Associate Editor of Advanced Science Letters. He is also a member of the Advisory Committee for the [[Cheltenham Science Festival]].

In 2007, he was a judge on the BBC [[Samuel Johnson Prize]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Judges Announcement |url=http://www.thesamueljohnsonprize.co.uk/node/54 |work=The Samuel Johnson Prize for Non-Fiction |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=25 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225034228/https://www.thesamueljohnsonprize.co.uk/node/54 |url-status=dead }}</ref> for non-fiction and has been a celebrity judge at the National Science & Engineering Competition Finals at The Big Bang Fair. He was appointed Officer of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2008 Birthday Honours]].<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=58729 |date=14 June 2008 |page=9 |supp=y}}</ref> In 2012, he delivered the [[Gifford Lectures]] on ''Alan Turing: Legacy of a Code Breaker'' at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gifford Lectures |url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/arts-humanities-soc-sci/news-events/lectures/gifford-lectures |website=ed.ac.uk |date=23 May 2024 |publisher=University of Edinburgh |access-date=30 March 2024 |archive-date=14 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314223809/https://www.ed.ac.uk/arts-humanities-soc-sci/news-events/lectures/gifford-lectures |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2013 he was awarded an Honorary Degree (DSc) from the University of London.<ref name="rhul" /> Al-Khalili was elected as a [[List of fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2018|Fellow of the Royal Society in 2018]]<ref name="FRS 2018">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2018/05/distinguished-scientists-elected-fellows-royal-society-2018/ |title=Distinguished scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |date=9 May 2018 |access-date=9 May 2018 |archive-date=9 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180509221228/https://royalsociety.org/news/2018/05/distinguished-scientists-elected-fellows-royal-society-2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] in 2023.<ref name="NF23">{{cite web |title=Royal Academy of Engineering welcomes 73 new Fellows |url=https://raeng.org.uk/news/royal-academy-of-engineering-welcomes-73-new-fellows |access-date=4 October 2023 |archive-date=2 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231002080512/https://raeng.org.uk/news/royal-academy-of-engineering-welcomes-73-new-fellows |url-status=live }}</ref>

He was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2021 Birthday Honours]] for services to science and public engagement in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]].<ref name="GazetteCBE">{{London Gazette|issue=63377|supp=y|page=B9|date=12 June 2021}}</ref>

=== Broadcasting ===
As a broadcaster, Al-Khalili is frequently on television and radio and also writes articles for the British press.<ref name="imdb">{{IMDb name|2629380}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.journalisted.com/jim-alkhalili |title=Jim Al-Khalili |work=Journalisted |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120814195627/http://journalisted.com/jim-alkhalili |archive-date=14 August 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2004, he co-presented the [[Channel 4]] documentary ''The Riddle of Einstein's Brain'', produced by [[Icon Films]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=C4 to unlock secrets of Einstein's brain |url=http://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/c4-to-unlock-secrets-of-einsteins-brain/1094951.article |date=17 June 2004 |magazine=[[Broadcast (magazine)|Broadcast]] |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=27 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227032528/https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/c4-to-unlock-secrets-of-einsteins-brain/1094951.article |url-status=live }}</ref> His big break as a presenter came in 2007 with ''Atom'', a three-part series on [[BBC Four]] about the history of our understanding of the atom and atomic physics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rationalist.org.uk/articles/4070/facing-the-future-an-interview-with-jim-al-khalili |title=Facing the future: an interview with Jim Al-Khalili |date=7 March 2013 |access-date=2 November 2013 |first=Caspar |last=Melville |work=Rationalist Association |archive-date=11 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811010619/https://rationalist.org.uk/articles/4070/facing-the-future-an-interview-with-jim-al-khalili |url-status=dead }}</ref> This was followed by a special archive edition of ''[[Horizon (British TV series)|Horizon]]'', "The Big Bang".<ref>{{cite web |title=Lost Horizons: The Big Bang |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00dcbqm |work=[[BBC Four]] |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=24 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024132447/http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00dcbqm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In early 2009, Al-Khalili presented the BBC Four three-part series ''[[Science and Islam (documentary)|Science and Islam]]'' about the leap in scientific knowledge that took place in the Islamic world between the 8th and 14th centuries.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/audio/2009/jan/12/science-weekly-podcast |title=Science Weekly: What has the Islamic world ever done for science? |date=12 January 2009 |access-date=2 November 2013 |first=Alok |last=Jha |newspaper=The Guardian |archive-date=9 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309033945/https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/audio/2009/jan/12/science-weekly-podcast |url-status=live }}</ref> He has contributed to programmes ranging from ''[[Tomorrow's World]]'', BBC Four's ''Mind Games'', ''[[The South Bank Show]]'' to [[BBC One]]'s ''[[Bang Goes the Theory]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bang Goes the Theory: Top five weird physics facts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p0070lzn |date=10 July 2011 |work=BBC One |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=8 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308204245/http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p0070lzn |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2010 he presented the BBC documentary on the [[history of chemistry]], ''[[Chemistry: A Volatile History]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1038/nchem.809 | doi=10.1038/nchem.809 | title=Television: Can we have some more? | date=2010 | last1=Docherty | first1=Paul | journal=Nature Chemistry | volume=2 | issue=9 | page=701 | bibcode=2010NatCh...2..701D }}</ref> In October 2011, he began a programme on famous contemporary scientists on [[BBC Radio 4|Radio Four]], called ''[[The Life Scientific]]''.<ref name="The Life Scientific">{{cite web |title=The Life Scientific |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/features/science-discovery/jim-al-khalili/#intro |work=Radio Four |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=2 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130302092017/http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/features/science-discovery/jim-al-khalili/#intro |url-status=live }}</ref> The first of this series featured his interview with [[Paul Nurse]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/physics/news/stories/2011/66047_jim_alkhalilis_new_science_series_starts_on_radio_4.htm |title=Jim Al-Khalili's new science series starts on Radio 4 |date=7 October 2011 |access-date=2 November 2013 |work=University of Surrey |archive-date=3 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103151722/http://www.surrey.ac.uk/physics/news/stories/2011/66047_jim_alkhalilis_new_science_series_starts_on_radio_4.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has since interviewed a series of notable scientists, including [[Richard Dawkins]], [[Alice Roberts]], [[James Lovelock]], [[Steven Pinker]], [[Martin Rees]], [[Jocelyn Bell Burnell]], [[Mark Walport]] and [[Tim Hunt]], and he has himself been interviewed on the show by [[Adam Rutherford]].

Al-Khalili hosts a regular "Jim meets..." interview series at the [[University of Surrey]], which is published on the university's [[YouTube]] channel. Guests have included [[David Attenborough]], [[Robert Winston]], [[Brian Cox (physicist)|Brian Cox]] and [[Rowan Williams]], [[Archbishop of Canterbury]].<ref>{{YouTube|u=UniversityofSurrey|The University of Surrey}}</ref> In 2011, Al-Khalili hosted a three-part documentary series on BBC Four entitled ''[[Shock and Awe: The Story of Electricity]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00kjqcv |title=Shock and Awe: The Story of Electricity |work=BBC Four |access-date=2 November 2013 |archive-date=8 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130808073728/http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00kjqcv |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2012, Al-Khalili presented a [[Horizon (BBC TV series)|Horizon]] special on [[BBC 2]], which examined the latest scientific developments in the quest to discover the [[Higgs Boson]], with preliminary results from the [[Large Hadron Collider]] experiment at CERN suggesting that the elusive particle does indeed exist.

Since 2016, Al-Khalili has been a regular contributor to the BBC Radio 4 series ''[[Curious Cases]]''.

Al-Khalili has been one of the experts interviewed in the [[Diane Morgan#Philomena Cunk|Philomena Cunk]] mockumentaries ''Cunk on Earth'' (2022) and ''Cunk on Life'' (2024).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnCJ1e-aaAk|title=Philomena Cunk meets theoretical physicist Professor Jim Al-Khalili &#124; Cunk on Life - BBC|date=6 January 2025|via=YouTube|access-date=8 January 2025|archive-date=8 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108124354/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnCJ1e-aaAk|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |user=jimalkhalili |number=1876971256576168063 |title=When I met Philomena Cunk {{!}} Cunk on Life fb.watch/w_aGD7QYWZ/ via @FacebookWatch |first=Jim |last=Al-Khalili}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.varsity.co.uk/interviews/27617|title=Jim Al-Khalili on Cunk and the powers of 'Edutainment'|website=Varsity Online|access-date=8 January 2025|archive-date=22 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240822205140/https://www.varsity.co.uk/interviews/27617|url-status=live}}</ref>

From September 2025, Al-Khalili presented the BBC series ''Secrets of the Brain'', investigating theories of the [[Evolution of the brain|evolution of the human brain]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Secrets of the Brain - BBC iPlayer | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/m002bbxm/secrets-of-the-brain | access-date=2026-07-28 | website=www.bbc.co.uk | archive-date=7 October 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007013701/https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/m002bbxm/secrets-of-the-brain | url-status=live }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
*2007 – Royal Society Michael Faraday Prize for science communication
*2008 – Appointed Officer of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in [[2008 Birthday Honours]]
*2013 – [[Warwick Prize for Writing]], shortlist, ''Pathfinders''
*2014 – RISE leader award<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/features/professor-jim-al-khalili-announced-rise-leader-2014/ |title=RISE Awards Announced |date=31 March 2014 |access-date=8 April 2014 |archive-date=2 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002165843/https://www.surrey.ac.uk/features/professor-jim-al-khalili-announced-rise-leader-2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2013 – Honorary [[Doctor of Science]], [[Royal Holloway, University of London]]<ref name="rhul">{{cite web |url=http://www.rhul.ac.uk/iquad/news/articles/hondegreesmarch13.aspx |title=Honorary degrees recognise contributions to science |access-date=2 November 2013 |date=26 March 2013 |work=Royal Holloway University of London |archive-date=3 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103111147/http://www.rhul.ac.uk/iquad/news/articles/hondegreesmarch13.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>
*2016 – Inaugural winner of the [[Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/jun/16/winners-of-inaugural-stephen-hawking-medal-announced-hans-zimmer-jim-al-khalili-particle-fever|title=Winners of inaugural Stephen Hawking medal announced|author=Nicola Davis|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=16 June 2016|access-date=7 December 2017|archive-date=8 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208231459/https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/jun/16/winners-of-inaugural-stephen-hawking-medal-announced-hans-zimmer-jim-al-khalili-particle-fever|url-status=live}}</ref>
*2017 – Honorary Doctorate, [[University of York]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/15403820.York_University_honours_global_experts/ |first=Catherine |last=Turnbull |title=York University honours global experts |date=12 July 2017 |newspaper=[[The Press (York)|The Press]] |location=York |access-date=13 July 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190210044354/https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/15403820.York_University_honours_global_experts/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*2018 – Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name='FRS 2018' />
*2019 – Honorary [[Doctor of Science]], [[University of St Andrews]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/graduation/honorands/ |title=Honorands 2019 |access-date=28 June 2019 |date=28 June 2019 |work=University of St Andrews |archive-date=8 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308155714/https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/graduation/honorands/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*2019 – Outstanding Achievement in Science & Technology at [[The Asian Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theasianawards.com/Jim_Al-Khalili.html |title=PROFESSOR JIM AL-KHALILI OBE |website=The Asian Awards |access-date=18 September 2019 |archive-date=5 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305170613/https://theasianawards.com/Jim_Al-Khalili.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

*2022 – Honorary [[Doctor of Science]], [[University of Birmingham]]
*2023 – Elected Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]]
*2025 - [[Humanists UK]] Darwin Day Medal

== Personal life ==
Al-Khalili lives in [[Southsea]], Portsmouth, with his wife.<ref name=tlsj /> They have a son and daughter.{{Citation needed|date=November 2026}} 

Al-Khalili is an [[atheist]] and a [[Secular humanism|humanist]],<ref>{{cite AV media |quote="I find it more comfortable to say I'm an atheist, and for that I probably have someone like Dawkins to thank." |people=Jim Al-Khalili |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/features/science-discovery/jim-al-khalili/#intro |title=Science Explorer: Jim Al-Khalili featured in The Life Scientific |publisher=BBC Radio 4 |access-date=15 September 2025 |archive-date=7 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250707193956/https://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/features/science-discovery/jim-al-khalili/#intro |url-status=live }}</ref> remarking, "as the son of a [[Protestantism|Protestant Christian]] mother and a [[Shia Islam|Shia Muslim]] father, I have nevertheless ended up without a religious bone in my body".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2008/jan/30/religion.world |title=It's time to herald the Arabic science that prefigured Darwin and Newton |newspaper=The Guardian |date=30 January 2008 |access-date=19 February 2010 |archive-date=11 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210911105403/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2008/jan/30/religion.world |url-status=live }}</ref> He became vice president of Humanists UK in 2016 after stepping down as its president.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Humanists UK Patron: Professor Jim Al-Khalili OBE|url=https://humanists.uk/civicrm/|access-date=9 February 2022|website=Humanists UK|date=7 May 2013|language=en|archive-date=11 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220611100044/https://humanists.uk/civicrm/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Al-Khalili is also a patron of the Guildford-based educational, cultural, and social community hub the Guildford Institute.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.guildford-institute.org.uk/about/ | title=About: Find out more about the Guildford Institute and its mission | access-date=26 September 2022 | archive-date=26 September 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926144455/https://www.guildford-institute.org.uk/about/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

== Publications ==
A list of Jim Al-Khalili's [[peer review]]ed research papers can be found on [[Google Scholar]]<ref name="googlescholar" /> and [[Scopus]].<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus id}}</ref> His published books include:
*{{cite book |last=Al-Khalili |first=Jim |title=Black Holes, Wormholes and Time Machines |year=1999 <!--isbn=-->|title-link=Black Holes, Wormholes and Time Machines }}

* {{cite book |last=Al-Khalili |first=Jim |title=Quantum: A Guide for the Perplexed |year=2004 <!--isbn=-->|title-link=Quantum: A Guide for the Perplexed}}
* ''The House of Wisdom: How Arabic Science Saved Ancient Knowledge and Gave Us the Renaissance'' (2010)
** a.k.a. ''The House of Wisdom: The Flourishing of a Glorious Civilisation and the Golden Age of Arabic Science''
** a.k.a. ''Pathfinders: The Golden Age of Arabic Science''<ref>Retitled to avoid confusion with ''The House of Wisdom: How the Arabs Transformed Western Civilization'' by Jonathan Lyons.</ref>
